skill.name: main-orchestrator
skill.description: Turns broad product requirements into epics, tasks, dependencies, and assignments for frontend, backend, data, test, and DevOps orchestrators.

content.value_statement: Complex feature requests often stall when teams miss dependencies across frontend, backend, data, testing, and DevOps. This skill converts requirements into coordinated epics, task assignments, success criteria, and progress tracking.
actual_capabilities: Breaks product requirements into epics with priorities, domains, tasks, dependencies, and success criteria.
Assigns tasks to frontend, backend, data, test, and DevOps orchestrators based on scope.
Defines validation checks for happy paths, errors, invalid input, edge cases, performance, and security.
Tracks progress through project task files and orchestration event logs described in the skill.
Guides conflict resolution for API gaps, circular dependencies, and limited execution capacity.
Triggers human documentation work when epics complete or architecture decisions change.
limitations: It provides planning instructions only and does not include executable automation scripts.
It depends on companion orchestrator skills and project state files being present.
It does not verify the correctness of generated implementation work by itself.
It should not replace human review for priorities, architecture tradeoffs, or release risk.

use_cases.title: Plan a Cross-Functional Feature
use_cases.description: Convert a broad feature request into scoped tasks for UI, API, data, testing, and deployment work.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Engineering Dependencies
use_cases.description: Identify task order, blocking relationships, and shared contracts before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Recover a Stalled Epic
use_cases.description: Review task state, resolve ownership conflicts, and re-sequence work across specialized orchestrators.

prompt_templates.title: Break Down a Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for one new feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the main-orchestrator skill to break this feature into an epic, domain tasks, dependencies, and success criteria: [feature request].

prompt_templates.title: Assign Work by Domain
prompt_templates.scenario: Route planned work to the right specialist orchestrators.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this requirement and assign tasks to frontend, backend, data, test, and DevOps orchestrators. Include task goals and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve Dependencies
prompt_templates.scenario: Fix blocked work across multiple teams or agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this epic for cross-domain conflicts, circular dependencies, missing contracts, and sequencing problems. Recommend a revised task order.

prompt_templates.title: Manage an Epic Lifecycle
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced coordination from intake through completion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an execution plan for this PRD. Include epic structure, domain tasks, risk controls, progress events, quality gates, and documentation triggers.

output_examples.input: Add OAuth2 login with Google and GitHub.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a high-priority authentication epic with separate UI, API, database, and end-to-end test tasks, plus dependencies and validation goals.

output_examples.input: The frontend needs an endpoint that backend has not built.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a mock API task, a backend contract task, an explicit dependency, and a logged architecture decision.

output_examples.input: Several critical tasks compete for limited execution capacity.
output_examples.output: The skill orders tasks by business impact, records delay reasoning, communicates priority, and updates timeline estimates.

best_practices: Provide a clear requirement, target domains, success criteria, and known constraints before decomposition.
Keep each generated task owned by one domain orchestrator with explicit dependencies.
Review task validation checks before implementation starts, especially security and failure cases.
anti_patterns: Do not create large tasks that span several domains without clear ownership.
Do not skip test requirements or quality gates to accelerate delivery.
Do not bypass task logs, state files, or decision records during coordination.

faq.question: What does this skill coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates product requirements, epics, domain tasks, dependencies, quality checks, progress events, and documentation triggers.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It plans and routes work to specialized orchestrator skills that handle domain-specific implementation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require other skills?
faq.answer: It is designed to work with frontend, backend, data, test, DevOps, and human documentation orchestrator skills.

faq.question: Can it handle single-domain requests?
faq.answer: Yes, but the skill recommends direct delegation when one specialist orchestrator can complete the work alone.

faq.question: What project files does it reference?
faq.answer: It references task state files, decision records, standards documents, and an operations log for coordination context.
